key_insight: Coupling parametric finite elements with symplectic Runge–Kutta time integration yields high-order curve evolution with provably exact enclosed-area conservation.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports accurate simulation of surface-diffusion-driven interface evolution without artificial area drift.
method: Discretize the classical BGN formulation using parametric finite elements.
Apply q-stage Gauss Runge–Kutta methods for temporal order 2q, without added conservation constraints.
Solve the fully implicit nonlinear system with an equivalent discrete formulation and monolithic damped Newton iteration.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests on various evolving curves confirm exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, with Newton iterations rapidly dropping below 8 per step.
watch_item: The fully implicit, strongly nonlinear solve adds implementation complexity; area conservation alone does not establish unconditional perimeter decay.
paper_title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
